hints: Look closely at the name peroxyacetyl nitrate, PAN. What element must gas M supply for this pollutant to form?
Remember the thermal decomposition test: nitrates release brown $\text{NO}_2$ gas on heating, while carbonates release colourless $\text{CO}_2$.
Now check the charges of the metal ions and the anions to see which listed formula is a real, stable nitrate that could release that gas.
walkthrough:
**Identify gas M from PAN**

Think like a detective. PAN is a photochemical smog pollutant formed when nitrogen dioxide reacts with unburned hydrocarbons in sunlight. So gas M must be nitrogen dioxide.

$$\text{NO}_2 + \text{unburned hydrocarbons} \rightarrow \text{PAN}$$

**Link M to compound L**

Nitrates decompose on heating to give $\text{NO}_2$, but carbonates give $\text{CO}_2$. So L must be a nitrate, not a carbonate.

$$2\text{X(NO}_3)_2 \rightarrow 2\text{XO} + 4\text{NO}_2 + \text{O}_2$$

**Check which formula is possible**

Calcium is $\text{Ca}^{2+}$ and nitrate is $\text{NO}_3^-$, so we need two nitrates to balance the charge: $\text{Ca(NO}_3)_2$. This is a real compound that decomposes to give $\text{NO}_2$.

options.A: Incorrect formula and so impossible. $\text{Ca}^{2+}$ needs two $\text{NO}_3^-$ ions to balance charge, so $\text{CaNO}_3$ cannot exist. Students who forget to balance charges may pick this.
options.B: Correct. $\text{Ca(NO}_3)_2$ is a valid calcium nitrate. On heating it decomposes: $2\text{Ca(NO}_3)_2 \rightarrow 2\text{CaO} + 4\text{NO}_2 + \text{O}_2$, giving $\text{NO}_2$ (gas M) which then forms PAN.
options.C: Valid formula but wrong gas. $\text{MgCO}_3$ is magnesium carbonate and decomposes to $\text{MgO} + \text{CO}_2$. $\text{CO}_2$ contains no nitrogen so cannot form peroxyacetyl nitrate.
options.D: Impossible formula. $\text{Mg}^{2+}$ and $\text{CO}_3^{2-}$ balance 1:1 to give $\text{MgCO}_3$, so $\text{Mg(CO}_3)_2$ cannot exist. It would also give $\text{CO}_2$, not a nitrogen-containing gas.
